name: get the intended change approved before implementing it
about: The gate before any code. Write the summary IN YOUR OWN CHAT — that is what he reads — in the bullet format `sb presets design-gate` prints, then `sb block` with one short line naming what you are waiting for. Two sections, and they are this step's own names for them. FIRST, Scope & Objectives: the scope is yours to derive, what the work covers; the objectives are HIS, inferred from what he actually asked for and restated so nothing he wanted goes missing. SECOND, the Change Contract, bulletpointed and high-level only — no implementation detail, no jargon, nested where the nesting means something. Order it for READING and not for building: he goes top to bottom once, and should finish knowing what the change looks like at a high level, what behaviour changes and which modules are touched, with little context on this codebase. He answers approve, or rejects with changes. ON A REJECTION YOU REDO THE DESIGN WORK — re-derive the scope, re-infer the objectives, rebuild the contract — and then summarise and block again; editing the wording of a summary he rejected is answering a different question from the one he asked. Bump `tries` and put the step back to `open` each time round. When he approves, put the FULL approved text — both sections, entire — in the step's `output` field, by hand in the plan file, because that is what the PR comment dumps, and only then tick. Write it there as MARKDOWN-READY NESTING — two-space indents under `-` — rather than as the `-`/`---`/`-----` marker levels you wrote in chat, so the PR comment renders as the nested bullets he read. This step comes BEFORE implementation and is an early root of the plan, whatever order it was added in — check its deps say so. Obliges `review`, which is where the contract you got approved is checked against what was built. A trivially small change skips this with the reason in `why`: a behavioural contract for a typo is a block nobody wants.
